newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-JUDEN TWO HITS CARDINALS IN MONTREAL WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-JUDEN TWO HITS CARDINALS IN MONTREAL WIN.

text.p: Jeff Juden combined with two relievers on a two-hitter and Henry Rodriguez doubled, tripled and homered to lead the Montreal Expos to a 4-1 victory over the St Louis Cardinals on Wednesday.
Juden gave up two hits over seven innings with two walks and four strikeouts. He did not allow a hit after Gary Gaetti's two-out single in the second and retired the last eight batters he faced.
"Juden pitched a great game," Expos manager Felipe Alou said. "After the first inning he seemed to gain velocity. He threw some late-inning fastballs that you don't often see."
Omar Daal retired the side in the eighth and Lee Smith worked a perfect ninth for his 474th career save and first for Montreal.
Rodriguez had an RBI double in the first, tripled off the top of the right-field fence in the sixth and homered off reliever Lance Painter in the eighth for his second RBI.
Chris Widger hit his first National League homer for the Expos.

In Los Angeles, Raul Mondesi hit a three-run homer in the first inning and had four RBI and Hideo Nomo allowed one run over seven innings to lead the Dodgers to a 5-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Nomo gave up four hits, including a solo homer by Mike Lieberthal in the fifth, struck out eight and walked none.
Mondesi connected on a 1-0 pitch from loser Calvin Maduro to give the Dodgers a 3-0 lead. He added a run-scoring single in the fourth.
In Houston, Mike Hampton outpitched Greg Maddux and Billy Wagner got Kenny Lofton to line into a game-ending double play with the tying run on third as the Astros beat the Atlanta Braves 4-3.

Derek Bell had a two-run double in a four-run third inning for the Astros, who can beat a third consecutive Cy Young winner Thursday, when 1991 winner Tom Glavine pitches for Atlanta. Houston beat 1996 Cy Young winner John Smoltz on Opening Day. Maddux has won the top pitching award four times.
Hampton allowed two runs and six hits in seven innings, walking one and striking out three. Maddux went six innings, allowing four runs and 10 hits.
In Cincinnati, Reggie Sanders hit a three-run homer in the first inning and Dave Burba made it stand up with seven strong innings as the Reds beat the Colorado Rockies 5-3.

With Deion Sanders and Barry Larkin on base, Reggie Sanders drove a 1-0 pitch from Rockies starter Billy Swift over the wall in left-centre. Deion Sanders went 4-for-5 with an RBI single in the fourth.
Burba, who started last season 0-8, allowed three runs and five hits, walking two and striking out seven.
Andres Galarraga and Larry Walker hit solo homers for the Rockies.
At Florida, Al Leiter allowed two runs and four hits over five innings and Bobby Bonilla added a pair of RBI as the Marlins edged the Chicago Cubs 4-3.
Through two games, Marlins starters Leiter and Kevin Brown have allowed just two runs and five hits in 12 innings.
Bonilla had an RBI single in the first and plated another run with a fielder's choice in the fifth. Jeff Conine went 3-for-3 with an RBI for Florida.
Chicago starter Steve Trachsel was hit hard, surrendering four runs and seven hits in 4 2/3 innings.
In San Diego, Chris Gomez's two-out single in the bottom of the 12th inning scored Archi Cianfrocco with the winning run as the Padres rallied for a 6-5 win over the New York Mets.

New York's John Olerud, had singled home the go-ahead run in the top of the 12th inning. He also made a stellar defensive play to save the game in the 11th and hit his first National League homer in the sixth.
Sean Bergman, the sixth Padres pitcher, earned the victory after retiring Bernard Gilkey to end the 12th.
